turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. My son found out he got a zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Who decided that, Hale, and on what basis?
Before we start, I reread Owen's last three essays this morning.
This morning. So the zero went in on the third, and you're reading his work now. I'm writing that down.
He writes like someone who was read to every night. That was you, wasn't it?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
You've raised a genuinely thoughtful kid. I mean that.
Then why are we here? Either you have something with a date on it, or I'm going upstairs to the principal when we're done.
Which is why I'd hate for this to become a fight between two people who obviously both care about him.
It became a fight when the zero went into the gradebook before anyone picked up a phone. Show me what you have, or withdraw it.
